title: Fleet velocity attestation harness and customer acceptance playbook
creator: Alex Kim
description: Design and implement an end-to-end harness and playbook to measure and certify dedicated fleet throughput guarantees. Deliver a repeatable benchmarking methodology, telemetry contract, and a customer-facing acceptance checklist for signoff during Dedicated onboards.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity require deterministic throughput guarantees and a transparent acceptance process. Current artifacts are fragmented (ad-hoc scripts, one-off dashboards). This initiative consolidates measurement, reduces ambiguity in SLAs, and speeds customer onboarding with a reproducible, instrumented workflow.
goals: Provide a deterministic load harness that can replay tenant mixes and produce throughput/latency signatures
Define a benchmarking methodology that maps real workloads to capacity units (tokens/sec per GPU pool)
Ship a customer acceptance playbook with pass/fail criteria and instrumentation links
Integrate telemetry hooks so Console can surface per-run evidence for sales & SRE signoff
scope: Create harness that runs in Dedicated staging and production (non-destructive mode)
Support tenant-aware mixes: short-chat, long-context, embedding-only profiles
Produce artifacts: CSV/JSON evidence bundle, dashboard links, deterministic PRNG seeds for replay
Automate end-to-end run and verification in CI for new runtime/kernel changes
non_goals: Implement a full tenant traffic generator for live customer traffic (we will use replayed synthetic workloads)
Guarantee cost-optimizing autoscale policies across every customer profile (we will produce recommended policies)
harness_design: The harness runs as a controller job that orchestrates: traffic generator clients, a load coordinator, and a verifier. It uses deterministic seed-based workload generators, supports rate profiles (ramp, sustain, burst), and collects fine-grained telemetry via our tracing + metric ingestion. Runs produce an immutable evidence bundle (run-metadata, sample traces, token timing histogram, and load-driver logs) exported to an S3 bucket for audits.
components: Load driver (k8s Job + Go binary) with tenant-mix presets
Coordinator service that stages ramps and enforces steady-state window
Verifier that computes success metrics and assembles evidence bundles
Console dashboard template & saved queries for run visualization
CI harness to run smoke and regression benchmarks on PRs
benchmarking_methodology: 1) Define workload archetypes from customer telemetry (chat, assistant, streaming, embeddings). 2) Create representative request distributions and sequence-length histograms. 3) For each capacity profile, run ramp-to-steady experiment: 5m warmup, 15m sustain, 5m cool-down. 4) Sweep qps until tail-latency or error-rate breaches. 5) Repeat N=3 with different seeds; report median and 95th confidence intervals. 6) Produce capacity signature: sustained QPS, median token latency, p95 token latency, error-rate, and tokens/sec per GPU.
acceptance_criteria: Sustained QPS at agreed pool size within +/- 10% of target across 3 runs
p95 token latency under customer SLAs (example: <200ms for chat-short) during sustain window
No pod restarts attributable to OOM or GPU driver faults during runs
Evidence bundle uploaded and accessible to customer within 1 hour of run completion
Console dashboard shows run with annotated SLO breaches if any
customer_acceptance_steps: Pre-run: share run plan, tenant-mix, and knobs with customer (Confluence link)
Execute: run harness in customer-dedicated staging with customer observer access
Verify: run verifier and produce evidence bundle and dashboard link
Sign-off: customer, SRE lead, and Solutions Eng sign acceptance checklist
Post-run: publish findings, recommended autoscale policy, and any follow-up actions
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha runs across three representative clusters (2 weeks). Phase 2: Pilot with 2 customers to validate acceptance flow and tweak profiles (3 weeks). Phase 3: General availability and CI integration so every runtime change triggers regression benchmarks (2 weeks). Each phase will include runbooks for SRE and a customer-facing Confluence template.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic profiles may not capture edge-cases - Mitigation: collect customer traces and expand profiles before pilot
Risk: Harness causes load that interferes with production - Mitigation: default to dedicated staging and strict rate caps; production runs require opt-in and SRE approval
Risk: Telemetry volume costs - Mitigation: sample traces and compress evidence bundles; configurable verbosity levels
Risk: Non-determinism between runs - Mitigation: seed RNGs, pin model versions and runtime kernels for each evidence bundle
dependencies: Console: new dashboard template and saved queries (CONSOLE-1021)
Billing: evidence bundle artifact retention policy (BILL-44)
SRE: permission for staging fleet time windows
